purpose: Removes the need to trust a single placeholder cost/value assumption (reports/business_assumptions.json). For ANY real cost-per-call and value-per-subscription the business supplies, find the capacity_pct row whose breakeven_value_to_cost_ratio is closest to (real value / real cost) -- that's the data-driven capacity to operate at, no model retraining needed.
computed_on: final_model.joblib predictions on the test set (39.5% positive rate -- a crisis-recovery-period upper bound per split_config.json, so precision figures here should be treated as optimistic vs. a steady-state period).

breakeven_table.interpretation: Calling the top 5% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 1.5x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 10% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 1.5x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 15% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 1.5x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 20% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 1.7x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 25% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 1.8x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 30% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 2.0x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 40% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 2.1x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 50% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 2.3x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 75% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 2.3x cost-per-call.
Calling the top 100% breaks even once value-per-subscription is at least 2.5x cost-per-call.

worked_example: If Finance says a call costs $8 and a subscription is worth $200 net (value:cost = 25:1), scan the table for the row whose breakeven_value_to_cost_ratio is closest to 25 -- that row's capacity_pct is the data-justified calling capacity, not the top-15% figure used elsewhere as a untested placeholder default.
